data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for secure remote access to United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) information systems with secure devices.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) information systems

policy_statements.source_text: It is USDA’s policy to comply with Federal requirements to establish, implement, and enforce a policy on USDA information systems that facilitate remote access and devices used to access USDA information systems remotely.
policy_statements.target: USDA information systems that facilitate remote access and devices used to access USDA information systems remotely

policy_statements.source_text: This policy complies with the requirements of:
The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA);
cross_references: The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA)

policy_statements.source_text: Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems;
cross_references: Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems

cross_references: OMB Memorandum M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information

policy_statements.source_text: Telework Enhancement Act of 2010.

This policy serves as the foundation for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to develop and implement procedures for secure remote access to USDA information systems, and secure use of devices when used for remote access that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This policy supersedes DR 3580-003, Mobile Computing, dated September 24, 2013.
This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until it is superseded or expires.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their client device, remote access, and mobile work procedures with this DR and DR 4080-811-002 within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date
policy_statements.target: client device, remote access, and mobile work procedures

policy_statements.source_text: This DR uses the term “remote client device” in place of NIST’s “telework client device.”
Two categories of client devices defined by NIST and used in this policy are:
Personal Computers (PC) (e.g., desktops and laptops); and
Mobile devices (e.g., smartphones and tablets).
Note: The term “remote client device” in this DR encompasses any device in the two categories of devices used to access USDA information systems remotely.
policy_statements.target: any device in the two categories of devices used to access USDA information systems remotely

policy_statements.source_text: USDA desktop computers used only within USDA facilities to access USDA information systems do not need the same security requirements as remote client devices that access USDA information systems remotely.
conditions: used only within USDA facilities to access USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Section 5c addresses USDA desktop requirements when used in locations other than USDA facilities.
Devices used both inside and outside of USDA facilities must meet configuration requirements in this DR.
conditions: used both inside and outside of USDA facilities
policy_statements.actor_name: Devices used both inside and outside of USDA facilities

policy_statements.source_text: This policy uses the following terms as stated below:

“Controlled Unclassified Information” (CUI) replaces and encompasses all previous terms and labels for sensitive information, such as, for official use only (FOUO) and sensitive but unclassified (SBU).
The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) CUI Registry - Categories and Subcategories defines 23 categories of CUI;
“Domestic travel” includes travel to all 50 states and U.S. territories;
“International travel” refers to business trips, as well as permanent duty assignments in any country, territory, or commonwealth outside of the United States and U.S. territories;

“Virtual environment” encompasses all forms of virtual remote access components such as virtual machine, virtual device, virtual mobile device, virtual device infrastructure, virtual mobile infrastructure, and encrypted container that ensures Federal information is under USDA control and encrypted when necessary; and

“Wireless” refers to client devices, (e.g., laptops smartphones) and networking devices (e.g., access points) exchanging data through radio communication within a limited geographic area, such as an office building.
The USDA remote access infrastructure affords personnel convenient and efficient methods to use client devices to access USDA resources from remote locations.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA remote access infrastructure

policy_statements.source_text: However, client devices, when used remotely (e.g., outside of the USDA physical or logical boundary protections), introduce additional risks to USDA information and information systems; therefore, these devices have additional security requirements beyond those that apply to information technology equipment operating within USDA owned, leased, or controlled physically protected areas.

System owners that permit information systems to be accessed remotely through remote access infrastructure assets must safeguard USDA information from threats arising from the lack of physical security controls, the use of unsecure networks, and potentially compromised client devices used by personnel when working remotely.
conditions: that permit information systems to be accessed remotely through remote access infrastructure assets
policy_statements.actor_name: System owners

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel using remote client devices are responsible for protecting them and knowing how, when, and where to use client devices securely.
policy_statements.actor_name: Personnel using remote client devices

policy_statements.source_text: There are four remote access methods:
Tunneling: virtual private network (VPN);
Application Portal: such as virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), virtual mobile infrastructure (VMI), and bootable secure operating system;
Direct Application Access: such as Web mail, timecard system; and
Remote Desktop Access: such as used by Helpdesk/Tech Support for administrative access.
There are four client device ownership categories:
Government furnished equipment (GFE), also referred to as organization-controlled devices;
Personally owned devices, typically referred to as BYOD;
Third-party-controlled devices, which includes devices owned or controlled by contractors, business partners, and vendors; and
Unknown devices, which includes client devices owned or controlled by hotels, kiosks, friends, or family members.
Note: Third-party-controlled devices are permitted to access USDA information systems when permitted by contract (see Sections 5a and 5b).
conditions: when permitted by contract

policy_statements.source_text: Unknown devices are never permitted to access USDA information systems (see Section 8k).
This policy applies to:

All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and use or are responsible for maintaining USDA information systems remotely accessed by devices or virtual environments; and
policy_statements.target: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and use or are responsible for maintaining USDA information systems remotely accessed by devices or virtual environments

policy_statements.source_text: All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA and all information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA.
policy_statements.target: All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA and all information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This directive builds upon other USDA information security policies that address application and device security requirements; however, this DR emphasizes identifying security requirements to enable individuals to remotely access USDA information systems in accordance with DR 4080-811-002, Telework Program.
This policy addresses the security of systems that implement remote access methods, USDA information systems that allow remote access, and devices that are used for remote access.
policy_statements.target: security of systems that implement remote access methods, USDA information systems that allow remote access, and devices that are used for remote access

policy_statements.source_text: This policy complements other information security policies, programs, and procedures including:
The following DRs and Departmental Manuals (DM):
DM 3530-005, Encryption Security Standards;
DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems;
cross_references: DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3520-002, Configuration Management;
DR 3575-002, System and Information Integrity; and
DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management.
cross_references: DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management

DR 35xx-xxx, Scanning and Remediation of Configuration and Patch Vulnerabilities, forthcoming; and

cross_references: DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: Users should comply with DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving, September 7, 2010, which provides safety guidance about the use of GFE and driving.
policy_statements.actor_name: Users
cross_references: DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving, September 7, 2010
policy_statements.target: DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving, September 7, 2010

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements of DR 4080-811-002 that defines approved worksites for USDA, when those worksites may be used, and the conditions under which they may be used.

Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems such as those identified in FISMA, policies, directives, instructions, and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or the intelligence community.
policy_statements.target: requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems

policy_statements.source_text: Requirements and security controls for client devices will be included in all contracts and agreements with third parties including contractors, business partners, and vendors that require access to USDA information systems.
conditions: that require access to USDA information systems
policy_statements.target: all contracts and agreements with third parties including contractors, business partners, and vendors that require access to USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices that allow third-party-controlled devices to access USDA information systems or services will have contract requirements specifying that third-party-controlled devices implement the same or better security controls as Government furnished client devices.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: that allow third-party-controlled devices to access USDA information systems or services
policy_statements.target: contract requirements specifying that third-party-controlled devices implement the same or better security controls as Government furnished client devices

policy_statements.source_text: Government furnished desktop computers accessing or storing USDA information remotely will have the same information storage restrictions, configuration, operational, and sanitization requirements as laptops.
policy_statements.actor_name: Government furnished desktop computers
policy_statements.target: same information storage restrictions, configuration, operational, and sanitization requirements as laptops

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will develop, implement, and maintain procedures for remote access, remote client devices, and virtual environments that:
policy_statements.target: procedures for remote access, remote client devices, and virtual environments

policy_statements.source_text: Include security practices in all phases of remote access infrastructure and remote client device life cycles;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Incorporate remote access procedures into business continuity plans;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Integrate with other security processes such as risk management, security assessments, continuous monitoring, incident management, and system error handling;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Integrate with vulnerability management processes and requirements such as vulnerability remediation, application of security-relevant software updates (e.g., patches and anti-malware signatures), and system configuration hardening;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an active inventory of remote client devices, virtual devices, encrypted containers issued, and the user assigned to each device or virtual device; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: active inventory of remote client devices, virtual devices, encrypted containers issued, and the user assigned to each device or virtual device

policy_statements.source_text: Implement monitoring capabilities to maintain current, complete, and accurate configuration baselines and to detect and respond to unauthorized changes or anomalous characteristics occurring over remote access sessions.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will:
Encrypt all Federal information stored on remote client devices with NIST certified cryptographic modules and comply with DM 3530-005;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Store CUI only on Government furnished client devices and encrypted containers created as components of a USDA information system that has authority to operate; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Tiered remote access guidance limits risk by permitting the most controlled devices to have more access to USDA information systems and services, while devices with less control have less or no access.

The user’s home;

a. This policy applies to:
(1) All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and use or are responsible for maintaining USDA information systems remotely accessed by devices or virtual environments; and
(2) All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA and all information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA.
b. This directive builds upon other USDA information security policies that address application and device security requirements; however, this DR emphasizes identifying security requirements to enable individuals to remotely access USDA information systems in accordance with DR 4080-811-002, Telework Program. This policy addresses the security of systems that implement remote access methods, USDA information systems that allow remote access, and devices that are used for remote access.
c. This policy complements other information security policies, programs, and procedures including:
(1) The following DRs and Departmental Manuals (DM):
(a) DM 3530-005, Encryption Security Standards;
(b) DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems;
(c) DR 3520-002, Configuration Management;
(d) DR 3575-002, System and Information Integrity; and
(e) DR 3640-001, Identity, Credential, and Access Management.
(2) The following future DRs:
(a) DR 35xx-xxx, Scanning and Remediation of Configuration and Patch Vulnerabilities, forthcoming; and
(b) DR 35xx-xxx, Bring Your Own Device, forthcoming.
d. Users should comply with DR 5400-007, Text Messaging While Driving, September 7, 2010, which provides safety guidance about the use of GFE and driving.
e. Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements of DR 4080-811-002 that defines approved worksites for USDA, when those worksites may be used, and the conditions under which they may be used.
f. Nothing in this policy will alter the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems such as those identified in FISMA, policies, directives, instructions, and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or the intelligence community.

The USDA remote access infrastructure affords personnel convenient and efficient methods to use client devices to access USDA resources from remote locations.

However, client devices, when used remotely (e.g., outside of the USDA physical or logical boundary protections), introduce additional risks to USDA information and information systems; therefore, these devices have additional security requirements beyond those that apply to information technology equipment operating within USDA owned, leased, or controlled physically protected areas.

Personnel using remote client devices are responsible for protecting them and knowing how, when, and where to use client devices securely.
There are four remote access methods:
Application Portal: such as virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), virtual mobile infrastructure (VMI), and bootable secure operating system;
Direct Application Access: such as Web mail, timecard system; and
Remote Desktop Access: such as used by Helpdesk/Tech Support for administrative access.
There are four client device ownership categories:
Government furnished equipment (GFE), also referred to as organization-controlled devices;
Personally owned devices, typically referred to as BYOD;
Third-party-controlled devices, which includes devices owned or controlled by contractors, business partners, and vendors; and
Unknown devices, which includes client devices owned or controlled by hotels, kiosks, friends, or family members.
Note: Third-party-controlled devices are permitted to access USDA information systems when permitted by contract (see Sections 5a and 5b).
Unknown devices are never permitted to access USDA information systems (see Section 8k).
